rationale:
Issue #69 reports IkigaJSONEncoder emitting syntactically invalid JSON ({,{"a":"a","b":"b"}) when an Encodable's encode(to:) requests two keyed containers for the same object, and even names Sources/_NIOJSON/Codable/JSONEncoder.swift:292 as the fix site. The minimized production patch is exactly one hunk in that file's _JSONEncoder.container(keyedBy:), wrapping the comma/curlyLeft insertion and the end/didHaveContainers assignment in `if end != .curlyRight` so a repeat keyed-container request reuses the already-open object rather than writing a second '{'. That is a behavioral correctness fix to pre-existing encoding logic, not a feature or API addition; the patch touches no other file, adds no formatting, docs, or config changes, and post-minimization validation is PASS with retained_hunks == original hunk (1 of 1, 0 removed). Traceability is fix_commit -> merged PR #70 ('closes #69') -> issue #69, and the commit selected from the multi-commit PR is the production-only commit. The curator trigger patch differs from the upstream test solely by adding `let encoder = IkigaJSONEncoder()` to repair an undefined local; it preserves the custom Encodable with two keyed containers and the exact `{"a":"a","b":"b"}` assertion, and depends only on APIs (IkigaJSONEncoder, Encoder.container(keyedBy:), CodingKey) that exist in the buggy parent 216e30b2 — the fix introduces no new production API. Runtime evidence is machine-generated strict gates, all passing in both strict_original and strict_post_minimization: single unique selector Tests/IkigaJSONTests/JSONTests.swift::testEncodeWithMultipleContainer, buggy differential reproduction, fixed isolated/suite/reversed clean, buggy full suite failing only on the reproduced trigger, fixed full suite all green, 32-run matrix with 3 repetitions and 3 matching deterministic fingerprint groups. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so orlandos-nl/swift-json#69 duplicates no active registry entry, and it is the sole allowed_root_cause_ids value.

Issue #69 reports that requesting a keyed container twice from the same _JSONEncoder emits a second '{' and a stray comma, producing invalid JSON such as {,"a":"a","b":"b"} where Foundation's JSONEncoder emits {"a":"a","b":"b"}; the issue text even points at Sources/_NIOJSON/Codable/JSONEncoder.swift around line 292. The minimized production patch is exactly that: one hunk in _JSONEncoder.container(keyedBy:) wrapping the comma/curlyLeft insertion and the end/didHaveContainers assignment in `if end != .curlyRight`, so a repeat keyed-container request reuses the already-opened object. No refactor, rename, formatting, config, docs, or feature surface appears in the hunk, and original_hunk_count equals retained_hunks (1 of 1) with post_minimization_validation PASS. Traceability is fix_commit -> merged PR #70 (body 'closes .../issues/69') -> issue #69, giving verified_fix_issue_numbers [69], which matches the single allowed root cause id. The trigger is the upstream-added testEncodeWithMultipleContainer with one curator edit: adding `let encoder = IkigaJSONEncoder()` because the upstream test referenced an undefined local. The custom Encodable with two keyed containers and the exact-string assertion are preserved, and it exercises only pre-existing API (IkigaJSONEncoder.encode, Encoder.container(keyedBy:), CodingKey), none introduced by the fix, so it is a faithful in-repo restatement of the issue reproducer. Runtime evidence is machine-generated and green in both strict_original and strict_post_minimization: both revisions build, the declared selector fails alone on the buggy revision and passes on the fixed revision across 3 repetitions with 3 matching fingerprint groups, buggy full-suite failures are limited to the reproduced trigger, and the fixed full suite is all green. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so this root cause is not a duplicate of any registry entry.

risks: The guard keys off the shared `end` field; unkeyed (bracketRight) and singleValue container paths that also touch `end` are only covered indirectly by the existing suite passing, not by a dedicated regression test.
The trigger asserts an exact JSON string, so any future change in key emission order would break it for reasons unrelated to the defect.
The issue's second variant (container1 created and used, then container2 created) is not exercised by the trigger, so the trigger under-constrains the reported defect surface.
